items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Sections are well commented (e.g. '自动化验收接口'), but the business logic leans on one-letter helpers and globals: `y(c(o.payable) - c(o.refundedAmount))`, a global state object `S`, plus `$`, `f.r`, `rd` and `d`. This hits the single-letter-name cap.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: There is a clear split between the `Biz.*` layer and the render/UI code, and the API reuses `Biz`/`computeStats`/`importData`. But it is one ~1488-line file (over the 500-line cap), and one large delegated click `switch` builds confirm dialogs inline with HTML strings.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Import parses JSON inside try/catch and runs `validateData` before overwriting. `run()` wraps operations, and address and quantity are validated. Some magic constants remain (500-entry log cap, name length 30, the `1\d{10}` phone pattern written inline), and the catch is generic.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Every dangerous action goes through `confirmBox`: pay, ship, cancel (`danger:true`, showing the stock released and the remaining refund), refund (showing the amount), restock, import overwrite and reset. Coupon rules, a summary table, status tags with steps, toasts and plain-language errors are all present.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: `shopTestAPI` delegates to the same `Biz.*`, `computeStats`, `queryOrders` and `importData` that the UI uses. Money passes through cent helpers `c()`/`y()`. Stats are recomputed every call. `validateData` runs before replacing state, and bad imports leave the state unchanged (tested).
